Erica, Espectroscopía Raman e Infrarroja aplicado a Cosmogeoquímica y Astrobiología, is a research group of the Department of Applied Physics of the University of Valladolid. Emeritus Prof. Fernando Rull and Dr. Guillermo Lopez-Reyes lead the group and its area of specialization is the application of advanced spectroscopy techniques, mainly vibrational spectroscopy and Laser Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy, to planetary exploration.
Our group is currently participating in the development of instruments that are or will be on board of different missions to Mars. One is the RLS instrument that will be part of the scientific payload of ESA’s next mission to Mars, Exomars. Another is Supercam that is onboard the Perseverance rover of the NASA Mars 2020 mission, currently operating on the surface of Mars. In addition, the group is participating in the development of the RAX instrument onboard MMX mission to Phobos and in the preparatory plans for the Moon exploration. 
Besides, of the work in space exploration, Erica is currently participating in several projects with different industries as part of this group compromise with the technology transfer of advanced spectroscopy from the lab to the industry and society.

The Faculty of Materials, Metallurgy and Recycling, Technical University of Košice (FMMR, TUKE) is a dynamic faculty which operates in the areas of education, research, development, technology, and innovation and is focused on key areas in metallurgy, digitalization of metallurgical processes, materials research based on the development of hydrogen batteries, waste treatment and recycling. We are focused on preparing successful international engineers and researchers with strong technical and analytical skills, the ability to understand complex systems, good team workers with strong communication skills, and critical thinkers. We join science and practice. We work with industrial partners from different areas and negotiate with city governments and politicians to set similar goals. We participate as an important partner in projects dedicated to developing innovative technologies. We are involved, lead and work on projects reducing CO2 emissions in iron and steel production, developing new modern materials and nanomaterials for special applications in medicine and environmental protection, and seeking environmental approaches to recycling metal-bearing and nonmetallic new waste streams. We reflect on the trends of the European Union to reduce CO2 emissions in industry and on the circular economy, and we also work in collaborative multidisciplinary teams to achieve industrial symbiosis.

The research team at the FMMR TUKE has decades of experience in the preparation of metallic and non-metallic materials. Since 2016 is focusing on preparation and characterization of thermoelectric materials. So far, they have prepared several half Heusler alloy systems, a series of completely new material compounds for wearable thermoelectric modules. 
We have over 20 years of experience with diffraction and spectroscopic methodologies at synchrotron, neutron and FEL sources and mathematical modelling of ordered and disordered structures. 
We also offer expertise in Material analysis of components intended for the space environment, and we could be partner in project with our know-how in material sciences using light, electron microscopy (SEM, TEM, HR-TEM), X-ray or neutron diffraction and spectroscopy. Our team has experience modelling atomic structures using the reverse Monte Carlo method.

entityDescription:
Founded in 2020 with the goal of establishing Portugal’s first commercial spaceport, ASC is a 100% private and Portuguese-owned partnership between OPTIMAL Structural Solutions and Ilex Space. This collaboration combines complementary expertise: OPTIMAL specializes in the design and maintenance of metallic and composite structures, while Ilex Space leads the commercial strategy and international business development. Together, they provide ASC with a strong technological and commercial foundation, enabling a comprehensive range of services—from launch operations to re-entry and recovery support.

ASC has developed critical technical capabilities to operate and manage a spaceport on the island of Santa Maria to meet Europe’s growing demand for launch sites. ASC’s mission also extends beyond infrastructure development; from facilitating satellite launches to developing custom-built ground support equipment and navigating complex regulatory landscapes, ASC is dedicated to advancing European space capabilities. Its activities align with the strategic objectives outlined in the Portuguese and Azorean Space Strategies, positioning the Azores as a pivotal space hub in the Atlantic and a gateway for Europe’s growing space ambitions. The ASC is committed to fostering strong local partnerships, creating an effective and competitive value chain, and solidifying the Azores as a thriving space hub, while preserving its pristine natural environment. The company is currently hosted at Incuba+, in Vila do Porto.
Looking to the future, the Atlantic Spaceport Consortium is aiming to being an enabler of Europe’s growing space ambitions. By sustainably enhancing launch and return capabilities at Santa Maria and throughout the Atlantic region, ASC is poised to leave a legacy of flexibility, strengthened international collaboration, and expanded opportunities for Europe in space.
Atlantic Spaceport Consortium (ASC) secured a licence to operate a Spaceport in Santa Maria, Azores, Portugal.
This is the first ever Spaceport licence to be issued by the Portuguese Space Authority (ANACOM) under the Portuguese legal framework updated in 2024.
The Malbusca Launch Centre, located at 36º55’57”N, 25º04’12”W, offers several competitive advantages, including: low air traffic density, integrated into the Santa Maria Oceanic Flight Information Region (FIR), managed by NAV Portugal; low maritime traffic density and a vast area of the Atlantic Ocean that will allow for safe flights and re-entry; and the ability to use launch trajectories that will eventually allow space objects to be placed in commercially attractive orbits.
Located in Portugal, within the European Union, the Malbusca Launch Centre is positioned to contribute to greater European autonomy in access to space and to add value to the global space economy.
